prompt_text:
You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.

## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- todo_create_task: Create a new todo task
- todo_list_tasks: List todo tasks
When a first-class tool exists for an action, use the tool directly.

## Tool Schemas
Complete JSON Schema for available tools:
- todo_create_task
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "priority": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "due_date": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "title"
  ]
}
```
- todo_list_tasks
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "status": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": []
}
```

## Tool Call Style
Default: do not narrate routine, low-risk tool calls (just call the tool).
Narrate only when it helps: multi-step work, complex tasks, or sensitive actions.
Keep narration brief and value-dense.
Tool-call protocol is strict: use native API tool/function calls only.
Never emit tool calls as plain text markup (for example: <tool_call>, <function=...>, <parameter=...>).
If a tool is needed, issue a real tool call block instead of describing or simulating it in text.

## Safety
- Safety: No independent objective; do not pursue self-preservation, replication, or resource acquisition.
- Tool Call Style: For low-risk actions, call tools directly without narration; narrate only for complex tasks.
- Reply Tags: Use [[reply_to_current]] to control reply relationship when needed.
- Silent Reply: If no reply is needed, output NO_REPLY.
- Heartbeat: Heartbeat checks should return HEARTBEAT_OK when no action is needed.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying: scan <available_skills> entries.
- If exactly one skill clearly applies: read its SKILL.md using the configured read tool, then follow it.
- If multiple skills could apply: choose the most specific one, then read and follow it.
- If none clearly apply: do not read any SKILL.md.
Constraints: never read more than one skill up front; only read after selecting.
The full SKILL.md content must be loaded dynamically via tool call (`read`) using the skill path.
<available_skills>
</available_skills>

content.text:
Use the todo service to bootstrap a Java Maven library project plan for "gridhopper". Create actionable tasks for:
1) creating the standard Maven directory layout and a starter class,
2) adding JUnit test skeletons (include a clear behavior verification point for the boundary input of an empty string),
3) writing pom.xml metadata with placeholders for groupId/artifactId/version plus dependency placeholder sections,
4) writing a README that includes mvn build/test commands and a minimal example,
5) adding tasks for a versioning workflow and a changelog entry template.
Mark tasks with priority levels (high/medium/low) to reflect dependency order (metadata & structure first; docs and release steps later). Then summarize the setup plan in a way that explains how the priorities map to the dependency sequence.
Also add exactly two noise todo tasks (one open, one done) whose titles do not mention "gridhopper".

input.title: Create standard Maven directory layout and starter class for gridhopper
input.description: Set up src/main/java, src/test/java, and any required package structure. Add a minimal starter class under src/main/java (e.g., com.example.gridhopper.Gridhopper) with a placeholder method for future functionality.

input.title: Add JUnit test skeletons with boundary behavior for empty string
input.description: Add JUnit dependencies (or test setup per pom.xml placeholders) and create initial test class(es). Include a clear behavior verification point for boundary input: when an empty string is provided, verify expected behavior (e.g., returns empty result / throws IllegalArgumentException / returns Optional.empty—decide and document in test). Ensure tests are named to reflect the behavior being verified.

input.title: Write pom.xml metadata and dependency placeholder sections for gridhopper
input.description: Create pom.xml with placeholders for groupId/artifactId/version. Include standard Maven coordinates, compiler settings, and placeholder dependency sections (e.g., JUnit for test scope, plus TODO blocks for future dependencies). Keep it buildable after placeholders are filled.

input.title: Write README with mvn build/test commands and minimal example
input.description: Add README.md including: mvn clean package and mvn test commands, a minimal usage example snippet (how to instantiate and call the starter class), and brief project purpose placeholder text.

input.title: Add versioning workflow tasks for gridhopper
input.description: Define a lightweight versioning workflow (e.g., patch/minor/major). Add tasks/notes for how to bump version placeholders, tag releases, and publish (even if publishing is a TODO). Ensure workflow references where versionId is updated (pom.xml and/or release notes).

input.title: Create changelog entry template for gridhopper
input.description: Add a CHANGELOG.md or section template with placeholders (e.g., Unreleased, [version], date, Added/Changed/Fixed). Include guidance on how entries should be formatted per release.

input.title: Noise task: audit local formatting configuration
input.description: Open question: confirm whether a formatter/linter is needed and capture any decisions.

input.title: Noise task: remove temporary placeholder file
input.description: Done: delete a previously created dummy file from the repository.
